documents.title: Licensing Standards for Assisted Living Facilities, 26 TAC Chapter 553 (Subchapters B, D Div. 2, E, F). Used as the fallback because no single policy-review form exists.
documents.form_number: None. Regulation sections that enumerate required written policies, plans and procedures.

documents.version: Current codified chapter. §553.259 and §553.23 were read on the Cornell LII mirror of the TAC (§553.259 shows amendment eff. 12/6/2022). Text for the other sections was read from a third-party reproduction of Chapter 553 (CHA Seminars, 164 pp.), which says it only approximates the rule. Verify against the official TAC. documents.how_used: Source of every item in required_items. Items keep the rule's own numbering, for example 553.259(c)(4). Only policy, plan, procedure and program content is listed. Application forms, fees, ownership, fire-marshal papers, licenses and physical-plant construction standards are excluded.

documents.title: Assisted Living Facilities Checklist (ALF Health Checklist)
documents.how_used: This is the surveyor's compliance checklist that mirrors Chapter 553, and it is the closest official 'checklist'. Fetching the PDF failed, so it was not itemized. Use it as a cross-check against the items below. The HHSC ALF page also lists PR 2383 (Alzheimer's certification checklist) and the PR 2384-2389 LSC checklists.

required_items.text: Applicant (good-standing applicant requesting a license before the health inspection) must submit via the online portal: the applicant's policies and procedures; with evidence of compliance with §553.257(b) (Human Resources) and documentation that employees have the credentials in §553.253.

Applicant requesting Alzheimer's certification before the health inspection must submit for approval the applicant's policies and procedures required by Subchapter F, and documentation of compliance with Subchapter F and §553.257(b).

Fire Safety Plan: an ALF must establish a fire safety plan for the protection of all persons in the facility in the event of fire; in effect at all times; written copies available to all supervisory personnel; copy readily available within the facility.

The fire safety plan addresses: (A) evacuation to an area of refuge; (B) evacuation from the building when necessary; (C) special staff actions, including fire protection procedures necessary to ensure the safety of any resident.

Large Type B ALF plan includes the NFPA 101 'Procedure in Case of Fire' provisions (§19.7.2 existing / §18.7.2 new); plan reviewed at least annually and revised; employees instructed on duties at least annually and when revised; plan reflects current evacuation capabilities of residents.

Smoking Policies: an ALF must establish and enforce policies regarding smoking, even if the policy is that smoking will not be permitted. The policy must also address e-cigarettes and vaping devices. If smoking is permitted: designate smoking areas for residents and staff, and provide ashtrays of noncombustible material and safe design.

Fire Alarm System: establish a program to inspect, test, and maintain the fire alarm system per NFPA 72 (and NFPA 720 where CO detection is provided), executed at least every six months through a contract with a State Fire Marshal-registered company; onsite documentation.
Fire Sprinkler System (if equipped): establish a program to inspect, test, and maintain per NFPA 25, executed at least every six months; onsite documentation.

Oxygen: adopt, implement, and enforce procedures for resident use, storage, and handling of oxygen cylinders and liquid oxygen containers in the possession and under the control of residents, to ensure the safety of all residents.

Manager: designate in writing a manager with authority over the operation; manager qualifications, 24-hr management course, 12 hrs annual continuing education, 40 hrs/week on duty; designate in writing an employee competent and authorized to act in the manager's absence.

Staffing: develop and implement staffing policies which require staffing ratios based upon the needs of residents as identified in service plans; disclose the normal 24-hr staffing pattern to prospective residents and post it monthly; sufficient staff for items (A)-(F); night-shift staffing by Type A/Type B and facility size.

Orientation: all staff complete 4 hrs before assuming job responsibilities, covering at minimum: (A) reporting of abuse and neglect; (B) confidentiality of resident information; (C) universal precautions; (D) conditions about which they should notify the facility manager; (E) residents' rights; (F) emergency and evacuation procedures.

Attendants: 16 hrs on-the-job supervision and training within the first 16 hrs following orientation, including (A) assistance with ADLs; (B) residents' health conditions; (C) safety measures to prevent accidents and injuries; (D) emergency first aid procedures; (E) managing disruptive behavior; (F) behavior management; (G) fall prevention.

Direct care staff: 6 hrs annual education, including 1 hr fall prevention and 1 hr behavior management (competency-based; addresses unique needs of the facility). Facilities employing licensed nurses, CNAs or certified medication aides: annual in-service training appropriate to job responsibilities (topics A-F).

Alzheimer's training for staff providing personal care to residents with Alzheimer's or related disorders in a non-certified facility: manager 4 hrs plus 2 hrs annual CE; personal care staff 4 hrs plus 2 hrs CE; non-direct-service staff training; competency-based evaluation; training certificates and records.

All Staff Policy: a facility must adopt, implement, and enforce a written policy that (1) requires a facility employee who provides direct care to a resident with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder to successfully complete training in the provision of care to such residents and (2) ensures the care and services provided meet the specific identified needs of the resident relating to the diagnosis.

Training under (a)(1) must include information about: (1) symptoms of dementia; (2) stages of Alzheimer's disease; (3) person-centered behavioral interventions; (4) communication with a resident with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder.

Personnel Records: keep current and complete personnel records including (1) criminal history check; (2) annual Employee Misconduct Registry check; (3) annual Nurse Aide Registry check; (4) initial TB screening; (5) compliance with or exemption from the facility vaccination policy; (6) signed statement acknowledging criminal liability for failure to report abuse, neglect, and exploitation; (7) signed disclosure statement (HSC §250.006 convictions; lived in another state in past five years).

Investigation of Facility Employees: comply with HSC Ch. 250; search EMR and NAR before hire and at least every 12 months, keep results in the personnel file; do not hire or continue to employ persons listed as unemployable or barred by HSC §250.006; give EMR notification per §561.3; name-based criminal history check in prior states of residence (no direct resident contact pending results); suspend employees found by HHSC to have engaged in reportable conduct while appeals are pending.

A facility must not admit or retain a resident whose needs cannot be met by the facility and who cannot secure the necessary services from an outside resource; additional services require written concurrence of the resident, physician, or legal representative.

There must be a written admission agreement between the facility and the resident specifying such details as services to be provided and the charges for the services; statement if services/supplies could be a Medicare benefit.

Share disclosure statement, rate schedule, and service plan with outside resources providing additional services; Memory Care Disclosure Statement (Form 3650) if the facility advertises memory care, and disclose whether Alzheimer's certified (Form 3641 if certified).

Health examination by a physician within 30 days before or 14 days after admission; secure at admission the identifying information in items (A)-(K) (name, SSN, usual residence, sex, marital status, DOB, place of birth, occupation, emergency notification contacts and physician, pharmacy preference, Medicaid/Medicare number).

Resident Assessment and Service Plan: within 14 days of admission, a comprehensive assessment (items A-T, e.g., location admitted from, primary language, sleep-cycle issues, behavioral symptoms, psychosocial issues, dementia history, ADL patterns, cognitive skills, communication, physical functioning, continence, nutrition, oral/dental, diagnoses, medications, special treatments, hospital admissions, preventive health needs) and an individual service plan; service plan signed by resident or responsible person and updated annually and on significant change; respite and emergency admission provisions.

Before admitting, explain and provide the disclosure statement and document receipt; provide the Residents' Bill of Rights; provide the resident's immediate family, and document receipt of, the HHSC abuse/neglect/exploitation hotline number.

The facility must have written policies regarding residents accepted, services provided, charges, refunds, responsibilities of facility and residents, privileges of residents, and other rules and regulations.

Make resident policies available to staff and to residents or responsible parties at admission, with documented notice of changes before the effective date; before or upon admission notify resident/representative of HHSC rules and facility policies on restraint and seclusion; give a written copy of the emergency preparedness plan or an evacuation summary.

Advance Directives: maintain written policies regarding implementation of advance directives, including a clear and precise statement of any procedure the facility is unwilling or unable to provide or withhold; give written notice to residents at admission (order of preference for incapacitated residents).

Inappropriate Placement / evacuation waiver: facility procedures for aging in place and inappropriate placement (Forms 1124, 1125, 1126; detailed emergency plan; evacuation waiver request within 10 working days); disclosure statement must notify resident of the waiver process and the facility's policies and procedures for aging in place; 30-day discharge if not obtained.

Medications: administration per physician's orders by authorized persons (licensed, medication aide, or RN-delegated employee); dispensing through pharmacy; medication profile record contents (name, strength, dosage, amount received, directions, route, Rx number, pharmacy, date issued); supervision limited to listed tasks; monthly counseling for residents who self-administer; immediate reporting of unusual reactions; written record of missed doses.

Storage: locked area for all medications; each resident's medication stored separately; locked refrigerator storage; poisons and 'external use only' medications stored separately; if controlled drugs are stored, facility policies and procedures must address the prevention of the diversion of the controlled drugs.

Disposal: discontinued, deceased-resident and expired medications kept separate and disposed of by a Texas-registered pharmacist; needles and syringes per 25 TAC §§1.131-1.137; release of medications to discharged residents on signed receipt.

Accident, Injury, or Acute Illness: arrange emergency care or transfer; immediately notify physician and next of kin/responsible party/placing agency; describe and document on a separate report with final disposition; stock first aid supplies for burns, cuts, and poisoning in a single location.

Healthcare Professional: coordination of services within scope of practice; facility must not provide ongoing services comparable to a nursing facility; residents may contract with a HCSSA or independent professional.
Activities Program: the facility must provide an activity or social program at least weekly for the residents.

Dietary Services: person designated responsible for food service; at least three meals daily with no more than a 16-hr span between evening meal and breakfast; menus planned one week in advance, followed, variations documented, records kept 30 days; therapeutic diets per physician order (calculated by a dietitian where required); four-day staple and one-day perishable supplies; food sources, storage, temperature, handwashing, sanitation, and employee-illness requirements (items 1-18).

Infection Prevention and Control: each facility must establish, implement, enforce, and maintain an infection prevention and control policy and procedure designed to provide a safe, sanitary, and comfortable environment and help prevent the development and transmission of disease and infection.

Report residents with reportable diseases to the local health authority; written policies for control of communicable disease among employees and residents addressing tuberculosis (TB) screening and a safe and sanitary environment; exclude infected employees from food handling or direct care; employee TB screening within two weeks of employment and annually; resident TB screening consistent with CDC guidelines.

Written policies and procedures for: (A) monitoring key infectious agents, including multidrug-resistant organisms; (B) wearing personal protective equipment and cleaning hands; (C) cleaning and disinfecting environmental surfaces; (D) using universal precautions for blood and bodily fluids; (E) removing soiled items from the environment at least once daily.
Written policy and procedures for making a rapid influenza diagnostic test available to a resident exhibiting flu-like symptoms.

Vaccine-preventable disease policy (HSC Ch. 224): written policy that MUST (i) require employees/contractors providing direct care to receive specified vaccines based on risk; (ii) specify the vaccines; (iii) include verification procedures; (iv) include exemption procedures for CDC contraindications/precautions; (v) include procedures protecting residents from exempt staff; (vi) prohibit discrimination/retaliation against exempt staff; (vii) require records of compliance or exemption; (viii) include disciplinary actions. The policy MAY include conscience exemptions and restrict contact during a public health disaster.

Restraints and Seclusion: all restraints for behavioral management, staff convenience, or discipline are prohibited and seclusion is prohibited; restraint only if physician-authorized in writing (circumstances and duration) or necessary in an emergency; behavioral-emergency definition; prohibited restraint types; acceptable restraint hold; post-restraint physician appointment and 24-hr notification; no retaliation for reporting misuse.

Wheelchair Self-Release Seat Belts: facility must allow use if the four conditions (A)-(D) are met; restraint-free facilities must give residents a written statement; circumstances when the facility need not continue to allow use.

Health Maintenance Activities (only if the facility allows personal care staff to perform HMAs without delegation): RN assessment per 22 TAC §225.6, documented conditions (stable and predictable; resident able to direct; written agreement), and reassessment at least annually (every six months for Alzheimer's residents); otherwise RN delegation under 22 TAC Ch. 225.

Resident Records: treated as confidential and safeguarded from unauthorized use, loss, or destruction; contents (A)-(H); available to residents, legal representatives, and HHSC; simple financial record of charges and of any personal finances entrusted to the facility; receipts upon request.

Guardianship Record Requirements: request the current court order and letters of guardianship at admission, when a guardian is appointed, and at each annual assessment; at least one follow-up request within 30 days; keep documentation and copies in the resident's record.

Residents' Bill of Rights: provide a copy to each resident and post it (in each resident's primary language); each resident's rights (3)(A)-(BB), including freedom from abuse/restraint, complaint rights, mail, visitation, financial management, records confidentiality, physician choice, service-plan participation, refusal of treatment, phone and privacy, personal property, Medicare/Medicaid notice by day 30, transfer/discharge limits and 30-day written notice contents, ombudsman access, advance directive.
Providers' Bill of Rights posted in a prominent place with rights (A)-(J); access to residents for HHSC and local authority employees.

Authorized Electronic Monitoring (AEM): permit AEM; do not refuse admission or discharge because of an AEM request; Form 3100 on admission, Form 0066 request, Form 0067 roommate consent; notice at room entrance; 8.5 x 11 'Electronic Monitoring' notice at main entrance; reasonable physical accommodation; abuse/neglect reporting for recordings.

Ombudsman access: allow the State Ombudsman, certified ombudsmen and interns immediate, private, unimpeded access to the facility, residents, resident-representative contact information, and records as specified.

Postings: license; HHSC complaint-procedure sign; inspection-report availability notice; most recent inspection report; Residents' Bill of Rights; Providers' Bill of Rights; local and State Ombudsman telephone numbers (800-252-2412); normal 24-hr staffing patterns; abuse/neglect/exploitation hotline sign (800-458-9858).

Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation: staff who have cause to believe a resident has been or may be adversely affected must report to HHSC (800-458-9858 / TxAbuseHotline.org) and local law enforcement; report must include (1)-(5) (resident name, age, address; responsible person; nature and extent of condition; basis of knowledge; other relevant information).
An ALF must follow its internal policies regarding the prevention, detection, and reporting of abuse, neglect, or exploitation.

Immediately make an oral report to HHSC, investigate the allegation, and send a written report of the investigation to HHSC state office no later than the fifth calendar day after the oral report; no retaliation for good-faith complaints; require staff, as a condition of employment, to sign a statement of possible criminal liability for failure to report.

Risk assessment: conduct and document a risk assessment for internal and external emergencies or disasters relevant to the facility's operations and location (e.g., fire/explosion; power, telecommunication or water outage; wildfire; hazardous materials; active shooter/bomb threat; flood; hurricane/severe weather; epidemic/pandemic; cyber-attack; loss of all or part of the facility).

Written emergency preparedness and response plan based on the risk assessment, addressing the eight core functions: Direction and Control; Warning; Communication; Sheltering Arrangements; Evacuation; Transportation; Health and Medical Needs; Resource Management. The plan must document EMC contact information, include a process for communication with the EMC, and the location of a current resident list identifying residents with Alzheimer's/related disorders, evacuation waivers, and mobility or special needs; notify the EMC of the plan.

Plan maintenance: current printed copy in a central location accessible to staff, residents and representatives; review at least annually and after events, with updates within 30 days of shortcomings, drills, or policy/rule changes; document reviews; written copy or evacuation summary to residents/representatives; notify residents how to register with 2-1-1 Texas; register as a provider with 2-1-1 Texas.

Core Function One, Direction and Control: designate the Emergency Preparedness Coordinator (EPC) and an alternate EPC; assign responsibilities to staff by function or position and describe how each staff member understands their role.

Core Function Two, Warning: procedures for notifying the EPC of a disaster; who the EPC will notify (including off hours, weekends, holidays); procedure for keeping persons in the facility informed; procedures for monitoring local news and weather.

Core Function Three, Communication: primary and alternate modes of communication; when to call 911; location of contact lists (representatives and emergency contacts, receiving facilities with written acknowledgements, HCSSA/professionals, staff, resident population); public status communication; procedure for notifying staff, residents, representatives, emergency contacts, HCSSAs, receiving facilities, drivers, and the EMC.

Core Function Four, Sheltering Arrangements: procedure for deciding to remain in the facility (access to medication, records, equipment, water and food including special diets; safe power and temperatures between 68 and 82 degrees F; sheltering staff); notify the HHSC regional office and EMC after deciding to remain.

Core Function Five, Evacuation: evacuation destinations and routes with a map; decision procedure with contingencies and a plan for pets/service animals; documented acknowledgment from at least one receiving facility/destination and one alternate; procedures and responsible staff (D)(i)-(x) for notification of HHSC and EMC, staff accompaniment, resident accounting and tracking, release of resident information, re-entry determination, return of residents.

Core Function Six, Transportation: arrangements for sufficient vehicles; staff designated to drive and communication methods; procedures for safely transporting residents, staff and others; safe transport of and timely access to oxygen, medications, records, food, water, equipment, and supplies.

Core Function Seven, Health and Medical Needs: identify special services residents use (dialysis, oxygen, hospice); procedures to enable continued services; procedures to notify HCSSAs and independent professionals of an evacuation.

Core Function Eight, Resource Management: plan for obtaining, transporting and storing medications, records, food, water, equipment and supplies; staff assigned by position/function; procedure to keep medications secure and at proper temperature; safeguards for confidentiality, security, and integrity of resident records.

Receiving Facility (only if the facility will act as one): plan must include procedures for accommodating temporary emergency placement from another ALF, subject to conditions (1)-(5) (capacity limits, safety, ability to meet needs, log, continuity-of-care items).

Plan training: annual staff training; train staff on responsibilities before assuming duties and when responsibilities change; at least one unannounced annual drill; offer and document training to residents, representatives and emergency contacts; document compliance.

Self-reported incidents: report fires (call 800-458-9858; Form 3707 within 15 days); report death, serious injury or threat from a disaster (call immediately; Provider Investigation Report Form 3613-A within five working days). Emergency Response System: administrator and designee enroll and respond in the format established by HHSC.
Certified Alzheimer's facility: manager/unit supervisor qualifications (age 21 and education/experience options) and six hours annual continuing education on dementia care.

Alzheimer's staff training: 4 hrs dementia-specific orientation (causes/progression/management; managing dysfunctional behavior; safety risks); attendants 16 hrs on-the-job training (ADLs; emergency and evacuation procedures specific to dementia population; managing dysfunctional behavior; behavior management); attendants 12 hrs annual in-service on Alzheimer's.

Staffing: employ sufficient staff to meet the needs of Alzheimer's residents; in large facilities or units with 17 or more residents, two staff members immediately available when residents are present.

Admission procedures, assessment and service plan: use Form 3641; establish pre-admission procedures (application process, interviews, home visits) to ensure appropriate placement; give Form 3641 to any inquirer; comprehensive assessment within 14 days and annually; individualized service plan within 14 days, updated annually and on significant change.

Activities program: planned and structured program with a balanced mixture of cognitive, recreational and ADL activities; individualized; daily offerings and minimum structured hours; employee responsible for activities (activity director for 20 hrs weekly in facilities of 17 or more residents); monthly schedule; six hours annual continuing education; special equipment as appropriate.

notes: Texas HHSC publishes no single policy-review form for ALF initial licensing. <cite index="24-2">HHSC's ALF page lists an ALF Health Checklist (PR 2382) among its resources.</cite> <cite index="23-4">The checklist items represent 26 TAC Chapter 553.</cite> I could not fetch that PDF, so the items above come from the Chapter 553 sections that require written policies, plans or procedures. How policies are reviewed: an applicant files through the TULIP online portal, and HHSC then conducts an LSC inspection. After the facility has admitted one to three residents, the applicant notifies HHSC that it is ready for the on-site health inspection, which tests compliance with the Subchapter E operating and resident-care standards (§553.23(f)). The manual is reviewed against those standards at that inspection. A good-standing applicant (six years of Type A/B operation, no harm or sanction history) can instead request a license before the health inspection. That applicant must upload the policies and procedures plus evidence of §553.257(b) compliance and staff credentials (§553.25(d)). <cite index="7-3">A good-standing Alzheimer's-certification applicant must submit its Subchapter F policies via the online portal.</cite> Suggested organization: one manual tab per section in the order of 'sections' above, with the Rule cite at the top of each policy so a surveyor can trace it. Include the HHSC forms the rules require (3647 disclosure statement, 3650 and 3641 memory-care and Alzheimer's disclosure statements, 3100/0066/0067 for electronic monitoring, 3707 fire report, 3613-A investigation report, 4719 fire drill report). Use the current HHSC versions of these forms. Caveats: (1) Text for sections other than §553.19, §553.23 and §553.259 was read from a third-party reproduction that says it approximates the rule. Verify wording and numbering against the official TAC. (2) A Dec. 2023 Texas Register proposal would renumber sections (for example §553.275 to §553.295), so confirm the in-force numbering. (3) Items marked conditional (§553.263 HMA, §553.275(m) receiving facility, Subchapter F, §553.104(h) sprinklers) apply only if the facility does those things. (4) Excluded from the list: physical-plant construction standards, license fees, ownership and controlling-person disclosures, fire-authority documentation (§553.19(c)), and pre-licensure training certificates. Contacts: LTCR Licensing 512-438-2630 (LTC_ALF_ICF_Licensing@hhs.texas.gov); rules and policy questions 512-438-3161 (LTCRPolicy@hhs.texas.gov).
